topic: Lazy async initialization vs synchronous execution in Tokio
principle: Decouple constructor allocation from async initialization to avoid panicking when Tokio runtime handles are used inside an already-running runtime. Never call `block_on` or spawn a new runtime inside a Tokio task; instead, use a lazy handle (e.g. `tokio::sync::OnceCell` or `Option<T>` that is initialized on first async access) to defer work until the async context is available.
instruction: When building a struct that wraps a Tokio runtime or async resource, avoid initializing it eagerly in `new()` if `new()` is called from within an async task. Instead, store an un-initialized placeholder and initialize it on first use via an async method or `OnceCell`.
